title: Batch lifecycle surgery and KV cache coherence upgrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor continuous batching lifecycle and overhaul KV cache coherence to remove races, reduce tail latency, and simplify scheduler responsibilities. Deliverables: 1) new lifecycle state machine for batcher (clear start/commit/drain phases), 2) epoch-based KV cache invalidation with lease semantics, 3) simplified slot allocator with fewer lock domains, 4) migration shim for live clusters and stepwise rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests cover new state transitions and lease timeouts
No regressions on existing canary workloads (latency/throughput within 3% of baseline)
Canary rollout to 1% then gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback on SLO breach
KV cache evictions no longer cause duplicate model requests for the same session (observed drop in duplicate fetch metric)
New metrics (batch_lifecycle_state, kvcache_epoch, slot_alloc_failures) emit and are wired into dashboards
work_log: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Verified root cause: overlapping commit path in continuous-batcher and stale KV entries causing double-inflight requests under GC pressure. Recorded initial microbenchmark: median latency unchanged, p99 +18% under 75% load.

2026-02-20 - Miguel Torres: Design doc created: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/RUNTIME/Batch+Lifecycle+Surgery. Proposed epoch-based invalidation and lightweight lease tokens to avoid global locks.

2026-02-23 - Design review: Decided to decouple commit visibility from eviction path by introducing an epoch counter stored with KV shards and a short lease policy (50-200ms tunable). Trade-off: small increase in metadata writes for much lower contention and simpler invariants.

2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Agreed rollback plan. Implement feature flag runtime.batcher.new_lifecycle, default off. Canary path uses feature flag routing in ingress for 1% of requests. Metrics tracked during canary: p50/p95/p99 latency, duplicate_kv_fetches, slot_alloc_rate.

2026-03-01 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427 (batcher: state machine refactor + kv epoch leases). Includes extensive unit tests and a migration shim to accept both old and new lease headers.

2026-03-02 - Performance run: microbench against internal demo workload shows p99 latency improvement of ~12% and throughput uplift ~18% with new lifecycle and epoch-based cache under synthetic KV churn. CPU utilization down ~9% on serving machines.
2026-03-02 - QA note: Found a race when a slot is preempted during drain -> commit transition. Added guard in slot allocator and created flaky test to reproduce. Target fix added to PR.
2026-03-02 - Miguel Torres: Marked In Progress. Next steps: finalize PR, run full canary, update dashboards and runbook, schedule post-deploy monitoring window and retrospective.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Canary may expose unseen slow-paths on customer workloads. Mitigation: 1% canary, automated SLO rollback, extended monitoring for 48 hours before ramping.
Risk: Metadata write amplification from epoch writes. Mitigation: batch epoch bumping with debounce and validate write amplification on staging; fallback to lease TTL tuning.
Risk: Incompatible clients reading older lease header. Mitigation: migration shim accepts both headers and writes new header on successful responses.
Risk: Edge-case where drain+evict intersects causing missed commits. Mitigation: added test coverage and a conservative default lease window; manual mitigation steps documented in runbook.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge behind feature flag (runtime.batcher.new_lifecycle = false)
Step 1: Enable on staging and run heavy KV-churn synthetic load for 24h
Step 2: Canary 1% of hosted traffic for 6h; verify key metrics then keep 24h observation
Step 3: Ramp to 10% for 12h; verify dashboards and customer error channels
Step 4: Ramp to 50% for 24h; if stable, ramp to 100%
Rollback: Flip feature flag off and revert routing if p99 latency increases >5% or duplicate_kv_fetches spike >2x
qa_steps: Run unit test suite and new lifecycle fuzz tests
Execute integration test harness against multi-tenant replica with KV GC enabled
Run long-running soak test (72h) with simulated slot preemption
Validate dashboards and alert thresholds in staging before canary
notes: Follow-up: Consider compacting epoch metadata to reduce storage if write amplification is observed in production.
Follow-up: After stabilization, migrate the lease window logic into kvcache tuning advisor so Optimize can suggest optimal settings per workload.
Postmortem: Add to infra retrospective board if we encounter SLO regressions during rollout.
